newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Pride Fund seeks gay-friendly firms.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Pride Fund seeks gay-friendly firms.

text.p: In what appears to be a first for the industry, a new mutual fund has been launched that is being marketed directly at homosexuals and lesbians.
The fund buys only stocks of companies with policies it views as "gay friendly."
"We won't invest in companies unless they have a progressive policy towards gays and lesbians," said Shelly Meyers, portfolio manager of the Meyers, Sheppard Pride Fund.
The fund identifies such criteria as personnel policies that explicitly prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and companies that offer health benefits to homosexual or lesbian partners.
Two fund-tracking firms said the fund appears to be the first to have such criteria.

Meyers said that the firm has identified about 400 companies that met the fund's requirements, including about 200 in the S&P 500 Index. That's whittled down from a universe of about 6,000 U.S. public corporations.

Meyers said she has found that the technology, financial services and consumer services sectors have a higher proportion of companies that are "gay-friendly," with utilities and energy among the least friendly sectors.
Meyers said the fund's investment philosophy is value-oriented, seeking equities that are undervalued.

The fund uses a mixture of a momentum approach, scouring for companies with rising earnings estimates, a change in the product mix, or a significant management change. It also uses such traditional criteria as price to book ratio.

The fund has about 40 issues in the portfolio, and will always range between 35 and 55 stocks. Meyers estimated that the fund's turnover ratio -- or how often it sells stocks within one year -- will be relatively low, ranging between 30 and 75 percent.
Top five holdings are: Arrow Electronics Inc ; McKesson Corp ; Time Warner Inc ; Glendale Federal Bank ; and American Express Co.
Meyers said the fund has about $800,000 in total assets. New funds often find it hard to reach the first million dollars, but she said she expects to topple that barrier soon.
She expects assets to grow to about $35 million by next June. The fund is aimed both at individual investors and institutions.
Meyers said the firm has made distribution deals with Furman Selz and Co and Jack White & Co, and has been negotiating with Charles Schwab Corp about distribution.
